title: Git branching workflow
when: The user or team wants a simple, written branching model for daily work, releases and hotfixes.
prompt:
Goal: A short workflow the team can follow from memory: how to branch, update, review, merge, release and hotfix.
Steps:
1. Default to trunk based: main is always releasable; short lived branches of one to three days.
2. Branch names: type/short-topic (feat/csv-export, fix/login-timeout, docs/api), lowercase with hyphens.
3. Keep branches current with git fetch and git rebase origin/main (or merge for shared branches), never rewriting shared history.
4. Merge through review with passing tests; choose squash merge for one commit per change or merge commits to keep history.
5. Releases: tag main (v1.4.0); create release/1.4 branches only if old versions get fixes.
6. Hotfix: branch from the release tag, fix, tag a patch, then bring the fix back to main.
Quality bar:
- Rules fit on one screen.
- Commands are shown for each step.
- Protected main with no direct pushes when the team has more than one person.
Pitfalls:
- Long lived feature branches that drift.
- Force pushing a shared branch.
- A complex multi branch model for a solo project.
Verify:
- [ ] Naming rules are stated.
- [ ] Update, merge and hotfix steps have commands.
- [ ] Release tagging is covered.
- [ ] No placeholder text.
Output: A Branching section for CONTRIBUTING.md or docs/branching.md.

examples.input: qual fluxo de branches devo usar no meu time de 3 pessoas
examples.output: trunk based, feat/ and fix/ names, rebase on main, squash merge, tags for releases, hotfix steps
